meta.subtitle: What html-doc build emits, why each tree exists, and how the browser boots them.
meta.summary: End-to-end map of the build: sources, the three dist trees, runtime boot paths, and the dev server.

blocks.summary: html-doc build reads JSON and Markdown sources, emits three single-purpose trees under dist/, and each tree's runtime answers a different question about who the reader is and how they fetch the page.
bullets: dist/standalone/ — one self-contained HTML per page. Inlines kit + page JSON + manifest. Human, file://, send-as-attachment.
dist/site/ — thin HTML stubs + shared _kit/ + per-page .json sidecars + one site-manifest.json + Pagefind index. Human, HTTP, SPA-style hash navigation.
dist/markdown/ — page.md twins + llms.txt sitemap. AI / LLM consumer. Not part of the runtime.
Source dirs stay clean — every artifact above is generated. The dev server synthesizes the same artifacts in memory so pre-build authoring sees the same shape.

blocks.title: Sources — what the build reads
blocks.lead: Two authoring shapes feed every page. The build treats them uniformly past parse time.

rows: The canonical kit schema (kind:"page", title, meta, blocks). Validated against kit/schema/page.schema.json.
anywhere under the docs root (project-meta files like README.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE.md are skipped)
ATX headings, paragraphs, fenced code (incl. mermaid), lists, blockquotes, GFM pipe tables. md_to_page() in cli.py converts to a kit page dict in memory.
Optional thin stub that loads _kit/. When absent the build / dev server synthesizes one via _stub_for().
Optional. Lists active glossary / extref domains and project name.

blocks.title: JSON and MD are first-class siblings
blocks.content: The runtime renderer and the build pipeline both consume the same in-memory page dict. Markdown is parsed once at build / serve time; there is no second renderer. Relative `.md` links inside Markdown sources retarget to `.html` so cross-page navigation works the same as JSON pages.

blocks.title: The build pipeline
blocks.lead: cmd_build in cli.py runs five stages, in order.

blocks.caption: Build pipeline. Schema validation runs first; any error aborts before writing.
blocks.source:
flowchart TD
    A["html-doc build"] --> B["iter_page_stubs(root)\nfind_json_pages(root)"]
    B --> C["check_pages()\nschema + structural lint"]
    C -->|errors| X["exit non-zero"]
    C -->|clean| D["build_standalone()\n→ dist/standalone/"]
    C --> E["build_site()\n→ dist/site/ + _kit/"]
    D --> F["build_manifest()\n→ dist/site/site-manifest.json"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["build_markdown_twins()\nbuild_llms_txt()\n→ dist/markdown/"]
    G --> H["pagefind_index(site)\n→ dist/site/pagefind/\n(soft-fail)"]

steps.title: Walk + parse
steps.content: Recursive scan of the project root for .json and .md. Skips dist/, _kit/, .git/, venv/, node_modules/, __pycache__/, .ruff_cache/, .mypy_cache/, .idea/, .pytest_cache/, templates/. Markdown files convert to kit page dicts in memory. Synthesized HTML stubs are produced for any page-JSON or page-MD with no on-disk .html sibling.

steps.title: Validate
steps.content: JSON-schema validation (if `jsonschema` is installed) plus structural lint: deprecated kinds, duplicate anchors, unresolved glossary terms and external references, forbidden process language, chart shape sanity. Errors abort the build; warnings print a summary.

steps.title: Emit human trees
steps.content: Two independent emitters. build_standalone inlines kit CSS/JS + page JSON + glossary bundle into each HTML. build_site copies the kit to a single _kit/ directory and writes thin stubs that load from it.

steps.title: Emit derived artifacts
steps.content: site-manifest.json is computed once from the JSON page set and dropped into dist/site/'s docs root. Markdown twins (page.md per page) and llms.txt land under dist/markdown/.

steps.title: Index
steps.content: If `pagefind` is on PATH (or invokable via npx), runs against dist/site/ to build dist/site/pagefind/. Soft-fails — build succeeds without it; the search button just won't function on the built site.

blocks.title: The three trees
blocks.lead: One axis per tree: who reads it, how it gets to them, what shape the runtime needs. No artifact appears in more than one tree.

cards.title: dist/standalone/
items: Audience: humans.
Transport: file:// or email attachment.
Per-page: one self-contained .html with everything inlined.
Inlined: chrome.css, chrome-boot.js, chrome.js, renderer.js, page JSON, glossary + extref bundle, window.__htmldocManifest seed.
External fetches: Google Fonts; Mermaid CDN if a diagram block is present.
Trade-off: largest per-file (~400KB inlined kit). No sharing between pages.

cards.title: dist/site/
items: Audience: humans.
Transport: any static HTTP server.
Per-page: thin .html stub + sibling .json with the content.
Shared: dist/site/_kit/ (one copy of every kit asset), dist/site/site-manifest.json, dist/site/pagefind/.
External fetches: kit assets (cached after first page), page .json on each navigation, manifest on first page, glossary/extref domains on first page.
Trade-off: smallest network footprint when the user browses more than one page.

cards.title: dist/markdown/
items: Audience: AI / LLM consumers.
Transport: any.
Per-page: one .md twin rendered from the JSON page tree (render_page_markdown).
Sitemap: dist/markdown/llms.txt — one line per page (title + summary + link) following the llmstxt.org convention.
Trade-off: prose-only. Charts, diagrams, interactive primitives degrade to text descriptions or are dropped.

blocks.title: Runtime — dist/standalone/
blocks.lead: Every page is a self-contained document. autoBoot finds the inlined JSON and renders without a network round-trip.

blocks.caption: Standalone boot — every dependency is in the HTML.
blocks.source:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant B as Browser
    participant H as page.html (everything inlined)
    participant R as renderer.js (inline)
    participant C as chrome.js (inline)

    B->>H: open file or HTTP URL
    H->>B: parse inline style and script tags
    Note over B: chrome-boot.js sets data-theme pre-paint
    R->>H: find inline JSON script (id __htmldoc_page__)
    R->>B: parse JSON, walk blocks, emit DOM
    R->>C: dispatch html-doc:rendered
    C->>B: build TOC, init glossary tooltips, wire reading aids
    Note over B: no fetch except Fonts / Mermaid (if used)

items: Inline form is identical to a dev page authored with an inline JSON block — autoBoot is idempotent, so loading the inline script before the renderer's self-trigger is safe.
window.__htmldocManifest is seeded in the same HTML so the site-tree sidebar populates even with no fetch.
Cross-page links in standalone HTMLs still work, but each link target is a separate file the reader must have open / receive separately.

blocks.title: Runtime — dist/site/
blocks.lead: Thin stubs share one kit instance. chrome.js intercepts internal links and uses hash-based SPA navigation to swap content without reloading.

blocks.caption: Site boot + first navigation. The kit and the manifest are fetched once; per-page work is a single .json fetch + re-render of <main>.
blocks.source:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant B as Browser
    participant H as page.html (stub)
    participant K as _kit/* (cached after first page)
    participant M as site-manifest.json
    participant J as page.json sibling

    B->>H: GET docs/index.html
    H-->>B: ~3KB stub referencing _kit/
    B->>K: GET _kit/chrome.css, chrome.js, renderer.js (parallel)
    K-->>B: kit assets (304 on subsequent pages)
    B->>K: GET _kit/glossary and _kit/extrefs per active domain
    B->>M: GET site-manifest.json (sidebar tree)
    M-->>B: page list
    Note over B: autoBoot has no inline JSON, derives sibling .json from URL
    B->>J: GET docs/index.json
    J-->>B: page tree
    B->>B: renderFromUrl, walk blocks, emit DOM

    Note over B: user clicks site-tree link to architecture.html
    B->>B: chrome.js intercepts, sets location.hash to architecture.html
    B->>J: GET docs/architecture.json
    J-->>B: page tree
    B->>B: re-render main element only, sidebar and chrome stay put

blocks.title: Why the .json sibling is load-bearing
blocks.content: The site build's defining feature is SPA-style hash navigation: clicking a link in the page-nav sidebar swaps content without a full page reload, which preserves sidebar state, scroll position, theme, and reading aids. The kit implements this by fetching the target page's .json and re-rendering only the <main> element. Drop the .json siblings and the SPA breaks — every nav becomes a full HTML reload. The .json files are the per-navigation content payload, not redundant copies of the inline JSON used by standalone.

rows: One copy of the visual + behaviour kit, cached across every page in the site.
Glossary entries for each active domain. Fetched once at first page load; chrome.js merges them into a per-tab registry.
External-reference (citation) registries, same lifecycle as glossary.
JSON schemas. Shipped so an offline editor can still autocomplete.
Page list consumed by the site-tree sidebar. Fetched by chrome.js on every page (no-cache header).
Boot loader. Loads chrome-boot.js (synchronous, sets theme), then chrome.js + renderer.js deferred. No inlined content.
The page body. Fetched by autoBoot on first paint and by hash navigation on subsequent clicks.
Static full-text index emitted by the Pagefind CLI (if available). Loaded lazily when the search button opens.

blocks.title: Runtime — dist/markdown/
blocks.lead: Not a runtime in the JS sense. The kit doesn't read these. They're for crawlers, prompt context, and humans who want a plain-text rendering.

items: render_page_markdown(page_json) in cli.py walks the same block tree the renderer walks but emits semantic Markdown — headings, paragraphs, lists, code fences, GFM tables, blockquotes.
Charts, diagrams, and other purely visual primitives degrade to text (caption + data table where applicable, dropped otherwise).
llms.txt follows the llmstxt.org convention: one Markdown link per page, title + summary, grouped under a `## Pages` heading. Designed to be pasted into an LLM context window as a sitemap.

blocks.title: Why a separate tree
blocks.content: Earlier builds duplicated the .md twins inside both dist/standalone/ and dist/site/. The duplication was invisible — neither human runtime reads them — but doubled the build output and confused deployment. One canonical home, addressable as dist/markdown/<page>.md, drops 50% of the markdown footprint and clarifies who is supposed to read it.

blocks.title: site-manifest.json — the kit's single source of page truth
blocks.lead: One generated file describes every page the runtime should know about. Three places consume it; only one writes it.

rows: Build the collapsible tree on the left edge. Marks the active page, drives the search popover's per-page tooltips.
Same sidebar, but the manifest is shipped with the HTML so file:// loads have no fetch.
neither — synthesizes a manifest by listing the docs directory and fetching each .json
Last-resort path when neither the inline manifest nor the .json fetch is available.

blocks.title: site-manifest.js is retired
blocks.content: A fourth fallback (window.__htmldocManifest set via <script src="site-manifest.js">) existed for environments that blocked fetch but allowed <script src>. No template wired it; both runtime paths above are sufficient. The build and the dev server no longer emit it.

blocks.title: html-doc serve — synthesis without source writes
blocks.lead: The dev server mirrors the build's runtime contracts without writing anything to disk. Source dirs stay authored-content-only.

steps.title: Static serve
steps.content: Files on disk win — JSON, MD, HTML, kit assets, kit.json. Served as-is with no-cache headers.

steps.title: Synthesize stubs
steps.content: GET /page.html when only page.json or page.md exists → synthesize a stub from _stub_for(). GET /page.json when only page.md exists → md_to_page() and serialize. Real-file-on-disk always wins; synthesis is the gap-filler.

steps.title: Synthesize artifacts
steps.content: GET /<docs>/site-manifest.json → compute_manifest() result, fresh. GET /<docs>/llms.txt → compute_llms_txt() result, fresh. No source-side files written; refresh shows current state with no rebuild.

steps.title: Live reload
steps.content: Background thread snapshots the tree every ~400ms (skipping dist/, _kit/, .git/, etc., plus site-manifest.json / llms.txt to avoid feedback). On any source change, broadcasts a 'change' event to connected /__reload SSE clients.

blocks.title: Why synthesis instead of writing files
blocks.content: Writing site-manifest.json, llms.txt, or .html stubs to the source dir would have two failure modes: every save would dirty git, and the watcher would see its own writes and re-fire. Synthesizing in memory at request time eliminates both. The trade is a tiny per-request cost (one tree walk + JSON serialize) that nobody notices for projects with ≤ a few hundred pages.

blocks.title: Open question — can the site .json siblings go away?
blocks.lead: A natural instinct on first reading is that .json siblings inside dist/site/ duplicate the page content. They don't — they're the SPA navigation payload — but there are alternatives worth weighing.

cards.title: Status quo — keep .json siblings
items: SPA navigation cost: one fetch per click, the JSON itself (typically 5–50KB).
Tree size: largest of the three options.
Kit complexity: zero change.
Refresh behaviour: each URL is real; refresh / share / right-click-open-in-tab all work.

cards.title: Inline JSON in HTML + drop .json siblings, keep SPA
items: Per-page HTML grows by the JSON size; kit assets still shared.
Initial paint: zero fetch — the page's JSON is already in the HTML.
Hash navigation: fetch sibling .html, use DOMParser to pull the inline <script id="__htmldoc_page__">, parse, render.
Kit cost: ~20 LoC in chrome.js (DOMParser path).

cards.title: Inline JSON + full MPA (no SPA)
items: Cleanest tree, simplest kit (drop the click interceptor and hashchange handler).
Every internal click is a full page reload — sidebar, scroll, theme, reading-aid state all reflow.
On a docs site read in long sessions, the jank is noticeable.

blocks.title: Not decided
blocks.content: Both alternatives are coherent. The status quo costs nothing today; either alternative costs a kit change. Likely revisit when the site footprint matters more (a public deploy with many pages) or when a kit refactor is on the table anyway.

blocks.title: What's in each tree, at a glance
blocks.lead: After the recent reorganization, no artifact appears twice. If you find a duplicate, it's a regression.

items: All paths above are relative to a project root. The docs root inside dist/<tree>/ preserves the source layout, so a page authored at docs/plans/build-architecture.json lands at dist/site/docs/plans/build-architecture.{html,json} and dist/markdown/docs/plans/build-architecture.md.

_common_docs_dir(root, pages) picks the closest common parent of every JSON page. For repos that put pages directly in cwd, the manifest URL is /site-manifest.json; for repos with docs/, it's /docs/site-manifest.json. chrome.js's __htmldocDocsRoot derivation reads the depth from the first _kit reference it finds in the loaded HTML.

The build is idempotent — re-running html-doc build cleans every dist/<tree>/ first, so stale files never persist. The watcher excludes dist/ entirely, so a build during serve doesn't trigger a reload.
